Lorne Doerkson speaks during British Columbia’s election campaign on Sept. 28, 2026. His Conservatives won a majority in the Oct. 24 election. Credit: RoyalObserver/Wikimedia Commons
Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 26, 2026
The Conservatives’ landslide election victory in British Columbia has raised mining industry hopes for faster permits and stronger exploration incentives, while setting up a clash over plans to repeal the province’s Indigenous-rights law.
Lorne Doerkson’s party led in 63 of 93 ridings, against 28 for the governing New Democratic Party (NDP) and two for the Greens, according to Elections BC’s preliminary count updated Sunday. The Conservatives had 48% of the vote. Final counting is scheduled for Nov. 6. Outgoing Premier David Eby said he would resign as NDP leader after Saturday’s defeat.
“British Columbians have elected a government that has made mining a priority and our members are ready to help deliver on that,” Association for Mineral Exploration (AME) president and CEO Todd Stone said in a statement on Sunday.
For explorers and developers, the test is whether the new government can turn campaign promises into predictable approvals without deepening disputes over land and consultation. Red Cloud Securities called the result positive for permitting and investor sentiment but warned that repeal could shift uncertainty from the legislature to the courts.
Permit pledges
The Conservatives’ platform promises legislated approval timelines, a single review for each project and quarterly progress reports. Exploration permits would face deadlines matching or beating competing Canadian jurisdictions. The party pledged to expand the provincial Mining Exploration Tax Credit and press Ottawa to extend flow-through eligibility to engineering and feasibility work.
For operating mines and smelters, it promised competitive electricity and carbon costs, alongside fixed timelines for operating permits and mine-life extensions. Roads, rail and ports serving mineral districts would be treated as “provincially significant” infrastructure.
AME welcomed the permitting and tax commitments, while calling for reliable land access built on early partnerships with First Nations. Ahead of the election, the association sought amendments to the Indigenous-rights law and the Interpretation Act, rather than repeal.
The Mining Association of British Columbia (MABC) congratulated Doerkson and the Conservatives on their majority, saying the incoming government could help increase mining investment, government revenue and jobs. It looked forward to working with the government on responsible resource development, the association said in a LinkedIn post .
New projects
MABC’s policy priorities include faster permits, more funding for First Nations to participate in reviews, skills training and expanded electricity and transport infrastructure. The association identifies permitting delays as the province’s biggest barrier to mining development.
Its May economic assessment identified 31 proposed new mines and expansions across B.C., including 20 critical mineral projects. The association says the existing industry supports more than 56,000 jobs.
The Greater Vancouver Board of Trade urged the incoming government to reduce regulatory barriers to investment in resource and other major projects. It also sought permanent cancellation of the proposed provincial sales tax expansion to professional services and removal of the tax on machinery and equipment.
Shorter, fixed permit timelines could benefit developers such as Seabridge Gold (TSX: SEA; NYSE: SA) at KSM and Spanish Mountain Gold (TSXV: SPA) at its namesake project, Red Cloud said in a note on Monday. Tax incentives and clearer land access would matter more for earlier-stage explorers, it added.
“The change in tone is real and will lift sentiment quickly, especially among investors who have avoided B.C. over permitting and title,” Red Cloud said. “But that money leaves as fast as it comes.”
Rights dispute
The Conservatives pledged to repeal the 2019 Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act, known as DRIPA, and section 8.1 of the Interpretation Act. Their platform also commits to respecting constitutional rights and the duty to consult and accommodate First Nations where required.
DRIPA requires B.C. to align its laws with the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, while section 8.1 requires them to be interpreted consistently with it; AME says this has pushed even small exploration permits toward seeking First Nations consent, increasing delays and uncertainty.
The First Nations Leadership Council urged the incoming government to retain the Declaration Act, saying it offers a framework for reconciliation and certainty. The council represents the political executives of the BC Assembly of First Nations, First Nations Summit and Union of BC Indian Chiefs.
“We are at a historical crossroads: Battleground B.C. or reconciliation through the principles and road map of the Declaration Act,” Grand Chief Stewart Phillip, president of the Union of BC Indian Chiefs, said in the council’s post-election statement .
Duty to consult
Repeal would not remove the constitutional duty to consult, Red Cloud cautioned. Since March 26 last year, B.C. has required consultation before new mineral claims are registered, responding to a 2023 court ruling against the previous automatic registration system. That process is distinct from obtaining permission to drill or build a mine.
The legal dispute remains before the courts. The Supreme Court of Canada agreed on May 21 to hear B.C.’s appeal of a December ruling that its mineral claims system was inconsistent with the UN declaration, which the appeal court found DRIPA had incorporated into provincial law.
Investors should watch the first budget for the size of the exploration-credit increase and the legislature for permitting deadlines and any replacement consultation process, Red Cloud said.
“Whether this works out well for B.C. mining depends less on repealing DRIPA than on whether the new government can get permits out on time with First Nations on side,” its analysts wrote.

Las Médulas, famous Roman gold mining complex in northwestern Spain. ( Image by Rafael Ibáñez Fernández | Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0. )
By: Staff Writer October 26, 2026
Researchers have strengthened evidence that Roman miners used water to extract gold from Spain’s eastern Pyrenees, dating a long-suspected mining complex where an estimated 2 million cubic metres of earth were displaced, enough to fill about 800 Olympic-sized swimming pools.
The findings date sediments preserved in a reservoir at Les Guilleteres d’All, an archaeological site in Catalonia’s Cerdanya Valley. The workings left behind artificial ravines, trenches and a semicircular excavation about 300 metres wide.
Earlier surveys had identified remains of a water-management network that channelled water through gold-bearing sediments. Researchers from the University of A Coruña and the Autonomous University of Barcelona used sediment dating to establish a firmer Roman chronology for the infrastructure.
Roman hydraulic mining is already well documented at sites such as Las Médulas in northwestern Spain. The advance at Les Guilleteres is evidence of when the system was used, rather than the discovery of an unfamiliar mining technique.
Spain’s ancient mining districts continue to attract explorers. In the country’s south, Pan Global Resources (TSXV: PGZ; US-OTC: PGZFF) is pursuing copper discoveries in the Iberian Pyrite Belt, where its La Romana deposit remained concealed beneath younger rocks despite thousands of years of mining in the region.
Dating the mines
The study , published in the journal Land on Sept. 19, 2025, addresses a longstanding question about the mining complex: its distinctive terrain suggested Roman engineering, but researchers lacked firm dating evidence.
The findings do not establish whether commercially recoverable gold remains at Les Guilleteres. The research dates ancient mining infrastructure rather than assessing the site’s potential for modern production.
Excavations conducted between 2010 and 2022 uncovered part of a reservoir supported by a dam built from large stone blocks. An excavated section measured about 4.5 metres across and 1.5 metres deep, although the reservoir’s full extent remains largely unknown. The structure stored and regulated water needed to wash gold-bearing material from the surrounding deposits.
Sediment accumulated inside the reservoir during its final stages of use or after its abandonment, preserving evidence that could help date the infrastructure.
Quartz analysis
Researchers analysed two sediment samples using optically stimulated luminescence, a dating technique that measures signals stored in mineral grains, particularly quartz, after their last exposure to sunlight.
The study summarizes the results as placing sediment accumulation broadly between the second and fourth centuries AD, consistent with Roman occupation of the region. Drawing on the archaeological context as well as the dating results, the authors favour abandonment in the late second or early third century.
However, the dates do not establish when gold extraction began or precisely when operations ceased. They provide evidence for the infrastructure’s chronology rather than a complete operating history.
The scale of the operation nevertheless points to substantial engineering capabilities, although the researchers describe the workings as smaller than other Roman gold mines.
Hydraulic extraction relied on controlled water flows to break down sediment and recover gold particles. The process transformed the landscape, leaving excavation fronts and artificial channels still visible today.
Roman connections
The findings could also help explain the economic importance of Iulia Libica, a Roman settlement near the mines that corresponds to present-day Llívia.
The settlement was the only documented Roman city in this part of the Pyrenees, and researchers suggest it may have helped administer the region’s natural resources.
Ancient literary accounts had already pointed to local gold production, including a reference by the poet Martial associated with Iulia Libica.
Archaeological discoveries provide additional context. At El Castellot de Bolvir, researchers identified a metalworking workshop, while excavations at a nearby Roman cemetery uncovered a gold bracelet weighing about 23 grams.
Although these discoveries do not establish a direct connection to Les Guilleteres, they suggest that precious metals and metalworking formed part of the region’s ancient economy.
Researchers also identified a possible chronological relationship between the decline of mining and changes at Iulia Libica. Parts of the settlement appear to have been abandoned during roughly the same period as the hydraulic infrastructure.
The evidence does not establish whether the mine’s closure contributed to the settlement’s decline or whether broader economic and political changes affected both.
Further archaeological work could clarify how the mining network operated, when extraction began and whether gold production was administered through Iulia Libica.

By: Staff Writer October 26, 2026
The U.S. Department of Energy has designated helium a critical material, citing its importance to semiconductor manufacturing and growing risks to supply.
The designation, announced Friday under the Energy Act of 2020, recognizes helium’s essential role in energy technologies and vulnerability to supply disruptions. The department says the gas has no viable substitute in several applications, including semiconductor manufacturing, testing natural gas infrastructure for leaks and quantum computing.
“Helium is essential to producing the semiconductors and advanced technologies that power our economy,” Energy Secretary Chris Wright said in a statement on Friday.
Global helium demand is outpacing production, while limited refining capacity and lengthy permitting timelines constrain U.S. output despite substantial domestic resources, the department said.
Helium is largely recovered as a byproduct of natural gas processing. Its availability therefore depends partly on the development and operation of facilities producing the fuel.
U.S. sales of refined and gaseous helium reached an estimated 81 million cubic metres in 2025, compared with 80 million a year earlier, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. The country remained a net exporter, shipping 38 million cubic metres abroad and importing eight million.

Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 26, 2026
Mining shares could deliver outsized gains if investors shift even a small portion of their technology holdings into resource companies, Sarmaya Partners Fund Manager Wasif Latif says.
A slowdown in AI data centre spending could prompt investors to seek businesses generating growing cash flow, including gold and silver producers, Latif told The Northern Miner’s Western Editor, Henry Lazenby. The San Antonio-based investment manager who controls more than $35 million, sees parallels with the shift away from technology after the dot-com boom.
“And given the large size of the capitalization in the tech space, that’s a big, big elephant of capitalization that’s going to need to go through a tiny keyhole in the small capitalization of this space,” Latif said late Sept.
The potential rotation forms part of his “Return to Tangibles” thesis: inflation, national security spending and years of underinvestment could sustain a commodity upswing as more investors recognize the opportunity.

Mexican trucking companies launched an indefinite nationwide strike Monday protesting highway insecurity, cargo theft, extortion and rising operating costs, with demonstrations planned in major freight hubs along the U.S.-Mexico border.
The strike, organized by the National Chamber of Freight Transportation (CANACAR) and other trucking organizations, calls for demonstrations across Mexico, including Nuevo Laredo, Reynosa, Monterrey, Tijuana and Mexico City.
The protests could disrupt freight transportation through some of North America’s busiest commercial corridors, particularly in Nuevo Laredo, across the border from Laredo, Texas, the nation’s leading inland port of entry.
CANACAR President Augusto Ramos Melo said trucking companies have grown increasingly frustrated with cargo theft, violence against drivers, deteriorating highways, excessive towing fees and regulatory burdens.
The organizations are also protesting proposed changes to Mexico’s 2027 fiscal package that would reduce eligibility for a tax credit covering certain highway toll expenses.
The demonstrations were expected to involve truck convoys and vehicles stationed along highways, near logistics facilities and other strategic freight locations. Organizers have called for peaceful protests, although traffic delays and interruptions to freight movements remain possible.
Mexico’s Interior Ministry urged CANACAR to return to negotiations, saying several other transportation organizations had agreed to talks aimed at preventing disruptions to highways and commercial traffic.
CANACAR maintained its call for demonstrations despite the government’s appeal.
The strike comes amid mounting pressure on Mexico’s trucking industry, which plays a critical role in moving automotive parts, manufactured goods, agricultural products and other freight between Mexico and the United States.
The duration of the protests and their impact on commercial border crossings remained unclear Monday.
Why it matters: An extended trucking strike in Mexico could disrupt cross-border supply chains, delay shipments through major Texas and California trade gateways and increase transportation costs for U.S. importers and manufacturers.

The United States and Denmark have signed a maritime cooperation agreement aimed at expanding the U.S. shipbuilding workforce, attracting Danish investment to American shipyards and accelerating vessel construction and repairs through advanced technology.
U.S. Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg and Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen signed the memorandum of understanding Oct. 22. The agreement establishes a framework for drawing on Danish maritime expertise to strengthen American shipbuilding capacity and create new commercial opportunities for Danish suppliers.
Denmark is home to Maersk (OTC: AMKBY ), the world’s second-ranked ocean container line.
The partnership targets workforce training, maritime equipment and technology, and specialized services supporting ship construction, repairs and retrofits. It also calls for exploring local partnerships and joint ventures to help expand and modernize U.S. shipyard capacity.
The State Department described the memorandum as a first step toward a broader maritime partnership, saying it “will help create American jobs, strengthen U.S. security.” The department linked the initiative to President Donald Trump’s executive order on restoring American maritime dominance and the administration’s maritime action plan, which seek to expand shipbuilding capacity, develop skilled workers and strengthen supply chains.
“American shipyards need skilled hands, capital, and speed,” Helberg said in a social media post on X announcing the agreement. He said the partnership would support faster training, Danish investment and “quicker, cheaper builds and repairs.”
For Danish companies, the agreement opens opportunities to supply equipment, technology and services to the American maritime sector. The framework also seeks to strengthen maritime defense-industrial cooperation, including technologies and capabilities with both military and commercial applications.
The Denmark agreement joins a broader U.S. effort to enlist allied investment and expertise in rebuilding domestic shipbuilding capacity. Washington has established shipbuilding partnerships with South Korea and Japan covering investment, workforce development and production technology, while its trilateral ICE Pact with Canada and Finland focuses on expanding icebreaker design and construction capabilities.
The two countries plan to exchange knowledge and best practices on maritime policy and regulatory frameworks, involving government authorities, industry associations and other stakeholders. The State Department and Denmark’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs will lead implementation.
The announcement did not identify specific shipyards, investment amounts, individual projects or an implementation timetable, leaving the commercial scope and pace of the partnership to be developed.
Why it matters: The partnerships will deploy allied investment and expertise to help close workforce and production gaps while strengthening alternatives to China’s dominant shipbuilding industry.

Lula celebrates a historic fourth term victory as Brazilian president, triumphing over far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro.( Image courtesy of Lula’s official X account.. )
Posted By: Cecilia Jamasmie October 26, 2026
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s election victory is set to sustain the country’s push to process more of its vast rare earth reserves at home, with mining investors watching how his government implements new screening powers and industrial incentives.
Lula defeated far-right Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in Sunday’s runoff with 51.8% of valid votes against 48.2%, securing a fourth term overall, Brazil’s electoral court said . His next term begins Jan. 5. Bolsonaro has refused to concede.
“Lula’s win ultimately reinforces Brazil’s trajectory in recent years and, in particular, confirms the country’s critical minerals policy, which was launched in September of this year and is therefore still relatively new,” Juan Ignacio Guzmán, CEO of Santiago-based GEM Mining Consulting, told the Northern Miner Group’s MINING.COM.
The outcome leaves the administration responsible for implementing a framework that encourages domestic processing while allowing greater scrutiny of strategic mineral transactions. Its approach could shape foreign investment in Brazil, which holds the world’s second-largest rare earth reserves and is an increasingly important target for governments seeking alternatives to Chinese supplies.
“This country will not accept being anyone’s backyard,” Lula said in his victory speech , signalling continued resistance to pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump, whose administration has imposed higher tariffs on Brazilian goods.
Rare earth ambitions
Brazil’s critical minerals law , enacted Sept. 16, provides for screening changes in corporate control, significant foreign participation and international supply agreements that could affect national economic or geopolitical security.
The measures could complicate acquisitions and investment decisions, depending on how the government applies them.
Brazil holds an estimated 21 million tonnes of rare earth reserves, measured as rare earth oxide equivalent, trailing only China, according to the U.S. Geological Survey’s 2026 report . These materials are used in electric vehicles, wind turbines and defence technologies.
Foreign investors are already positioning themselves to develop that largely untapped potential. Subsidiaries of foreign miners and companies with foreign ownership stakes accounted for 42% of Brazil’s 2,727 rare earth exploration applications, an analysis by The Associated Press and Repórter Brasil of National Mining Agency records through June found.
More than 86% of the applications were submitted over the past three years, highlighting the rapid acceleration of interest.
US support
Brazil’s only large-scale rare earth producer, Serra Verde, was acquired by USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) in a transaction completed Sept. 3. The buyer has secured agreements for up to $1.6 billion in U.S. government support, underscoring Washington’s growing financial interest in the sector.
Guzmán said Lula’s approach would likely emphasize greater integration between mining and downstream industrial activities, particularly refining.
“If new rare earth mining projects are developed, the goal would ideally be not only to produce raw minerals or concentrates but also to carry out refining activities within Brazil,” he said.
Adriano Drummond Trindade, a Brasília-based mining lawyer and partner at Mattos Filho Advogados, said the industry’s principal concern is how the government implements the policy, rather than Lula’s re-election itself.
Investors are accustomed to government screening when it is predictable, consistent and timely, he said. The election gives the administration that negotiated the legislation in Congress responsibility for putting it into practice.
“As long as the three factors mentioned above – predictability, consistency and timely response – are adequately factored in the forthcoming regulations and in practice, the re-election shall not adversely affect investment in mining,” Trindade said.
A September decree established arrangements for the new minerals council, while the law leaves detailed screening procedures and incentive requirements to implementing regulations.
The government is also offering incentives to encourage processing and refining within Brazil. The law provides tax credits of up to 20% of eligible expenditures on mineral processing, transformation and urban mining — recovering materials from discarded products and waste.
The programme-wide ceiling is 1 billion reais annually from 2030 through 2034. Projects must qualify for government approval.
“The government is working to create a favourable environment for the establishment and expansion of beneficiation, separation, processing, refining and advanced materials manufacturing in Brazil,” the Ministry of Mines and Energy told MINING.COM in a written statement in September .
Washington ties
Lula’s victory leaves Latin America’s two most populous countries, Brazil and Mexico, under left-of-centre leadership.
Brazil, the region’s largest economy, with GDP projected at about US$2.6 trillion in 2026 according to IMF figures reported by Lusa , has resisted Washington’s demands despite increased U.S. tariffs.
The outcome contrasts with the approach advocated by Bolsonaro, who favoured closer ties with the Trump administration, including strategic cooperation on critical minerals.
Guzmán, however, does not expect the political differences between Lula and Trump to significantly disrupt cooperation in the sector.
“Brazil is currently viewed as a strategic partner of the United States in the global race for critical minerals,” he said. “Therefore, I do not anticipate any major repercussions in this regard.”
Guzmán sees scope for agreements combining U.S. financing, technology transfers and long-term mineral supply contracts with Brazilian industrial development. Such arrangements could help finance projects with tighter economics, provided domestic processing is technically and commercially viable.
“The Brazilian government should provide clearer and more stable regulatory frameworks regarding permitting, ownership rights, and supply commitments to the United States and other countries,” he said.
81 tomorrow
Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday, began his political career as a union leader before helping establish the Workers’ Party. He won presidential elections in 2002 and 2006, then returned to power after defeating Jair Bolsonaro in 2022.
Trindade said U.S. government agencies and private investors have continued pursuing opportunities in Brazil despite the new minerals policy and election uncertainty.
“Even if the Lula administration may want to increase screening and add requirements for local industrialization to a certain degree, such measures cannot simply scare away such investment that is so needed for Brazil’s mining sector,” he said.
“Given that mining investment is long term and high risk, the need for investment in the sector usually supplants political tensions.”

Ceva has deployed four car carriers, chartered by CMA CGM Photo: VesselFinder
By Alison Koo
26 October 2026
The orderbook for pure car and truck carriers (PCTCs) has surged amid booming Chinese vehicle exports and elevated charter earnings, raising concerns that an expanding fleet could outpace demand as European restrictions on Chinese vehicle imports threaten to curb a key source of cargo growth.
Greek brokerage Intermodal said last week that 82 PCTCs were contracted in the first nine months of 2026, compared with just nine vessels ordered throughout 2025 and a 10-year annual average of 35 vessels.
The orderbook-to-fleet ratio has consequently risen to 26%, well above its historical average of 14%, pointing to a substantial expansion in carrying capacity over the coming years.
CMA CGM boss Rudolphe Saade said in a recent interview with Lebanon’s L’Orient-Le Jour that the French line targets to have 21 PCTCs in the coming years. Currently, its 3PL arm, CEVA Logistics, operates 11 PCTCs.
Fuelling the surge in newbuilding orders is the growth in Chinese vehicle exports, which totalled 8.2m units in the first nine months of 2026, up 66% year-on-year.
However, the immediate impact is likely to be limited, with 64% of the orderbook, measured by tonnage, scheduled for delivery from 2028 onwards. This backloaded delivery schedule should help defer much of the supply pressure.
China’s rapidly expanding automotive exports have kept charter rates elevated, with ships being fixed for $95,000 per day, near levels last seen in 2024.
Subdued domestic demand and intense price competition have encouraged Chinese manufacturers to seek overseas markets. Domestic NEV sales contracted by 9.4% year on year, reinforcing the industry’s reliance on exports to absorb production.
The resulting increase in long-haul shipments, particularly from China to Europe and Latin America, has boosted car-mile demand, while limited backhaul cargoes and diversions around the Cape of Good Hope have lengthened voyages and tied up vessel capacity.
Yet the demand outlook faces mounting risks from European trade policy.
In October 2026, the EU and China reportedly reached a preliminary understanding on proposed restrictions covering Chinese-built conventional and plug-in hybrid vehicles. Under the proposed four-year arrangement, which could take effect in December subject to formal implementation, annual imports would initially be capped at 350,000 units, with the quota increasing by 6% annually.
Battery-electric vehicles would remain subject to separate EU anti-subsidy duties.
Intermodal said: “Against projected Chinese hybrid imports of around 800,000 units in 2026, these measures could significantly constrain shipment growth along the China-Europe corridor. The impact on car-mile demand will largely depend on manufacturers’ ability to redirect exports to alternative markets.”
Meanwhile, Chinese automakers like BYD and SAIC Motor are expanding their own shipping fleets, potentially reducing their reliance on vessels chartered in the open market. This could further alter demand for third-party tonnage even if China’s overall vehicle exports continue growing.

Collective Mining Executive Chairman Ari Sussman last month in Colorado Springs.
Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 26, 2026
Collective Mining (TSX, Nasdaq: CNL) aims to submit an environmental licence application for its Apollo deposit in Colombia by mid-2027 while continuing to drill beyond its initial resource, Executive Chairman Ari Sussman says.
The company has 13 rigs operating across its Guayabales project in Caldas department and plans another 120,000 metres of drilling at Apollo before a resource update is due by late next year. He said early engineering work would help shape development plans and reduce the risk of costly changes during construction.
“The number one lesson, bring the engineers in way earlier than you think,” Sussman told The Northern Miner’s Western Editor, Henry Lazenby, late last month in Colorado Springs. “Once you start construction of any mine, you can’t really change what you’re doing once it starts.”
Apollo’s first resource , released in September, outlined potential for both open-pit and underground mining, giving Collective more development options to assess. Sussman expects a preliminary economic assessment alongside or shortly after the resource update.

After introducing the updated RZ last year, the electric SUV has seen significantly more demand this year.
Toyota’s luxury brand sold over 10,000 RZs through September, nearly double (+91%) the 5,340 it managed during the same period last year.
For the 2027 model year, the Lexus RZ will be available with three powertrains: 350e, 450e AWD, and 550e F Sport AWD.

The F Sport variant is also the first to feature M Mode, an electronic system that replicates the feeling of an eight-speed manual transmission.

Inside, the RZ comes with NuLuxe-trimmed seats as standard, while the Luxury and F Sport grades have Ultrasuede-trimmed seats and laser-etched Ultrasuede door trim inserts.

source_document.body:
Japan Airlines has expanded scheduled transcontinental all-cargo flights, utilizing Boeing 747 freighter aircraft operated by three large cargo airlines to take advantage of surging demand for shipments of semiconductors and digital equipment, much of it to support the rapid buildout of AI infrastructure.
The Tokyo-based carrier began flying freighters again for the first time in 13 years in February 2024 and now operates three Boeing 767-300 converted freighters that previously flew for its passenger business. But those aircraft primarily operate on intra-Asia routes.
In a 2035 strategy outlined in March, Japan Airlines said it planned to add large freighters to the cargo business to meet robust demand between Asia, North America and Europe, especially for high-value cargo such as semiconductor manufacturing equipment and pharmaceuticals.
Towards that end, Japan Airlines has enlisted U.S.-based carriers Atlas Air and Kalitta Air, as well as Cargolux, to operate cargo jets under long-term charter agreements, according to a company news release earlier this month.
Kalitta Air operates Boeing 747-400s on JAL’s behalf six times per week between Tokyo Narita International Airport and Chicago. Kalitta replaced Western Global Airlines, the previous operator on the route.
Cargolux operates two Boeing 747-400s twice a week between Narita and Luxembourg.
Atlas Air operates twice per week for JAL between Narita and Los Angeles International Airport. Atlas Air subcontracts some of the flights to partner carriers.
JAL also procured Atlas Air flights to establish a dedicated network for Nippon Express Group, a major logistics customer to meet the growing demand for AI and semiconductor-related goods. The service operates on a circular route starting from Los Angeles, passing through Narita airport, Taipei, Taiwan, and Singapore and back to Narita before returning to Los Angeles, Nippon Express announced earlier this month. The service began with one flight per week and could be expanded in the future, it said.
Nippon Express said there is high demand for servers, server racks, semiconductors, semiconductor manufacturing equipment and other electronic componentst between Tokyo, Taipei and Singapore, but there are few airlines operating large cargo jets within Asia, limiting available options. The 747s, with about 100 tons of capacity, will provide a unique and highly valued capability, it said.
A recent analysis by Frost & Sullivan and FedEx quantified the huge production growth in semiconductor and AI-related equipment in the Asia-Pacific region, with an ecosystem of suppliers shipping components back-and-forth. Many end customers are hyperscalers based in North America. Logistics providers and airlines are racing to offer more services for the AI market because it offers very high margins.
Japan Airlines withdrew from freighter operations in 2010 as part of a bankruptcy reorganization. One of the motivations to restart the in-house cargo airline in 2024 was the boom in e-commerce. JAL primarily operates standard-size passenger jets on short-haul routes in Asia, but the planes don’t have sufficient capacity in the lower deck to meet cargo demand.

Someone Bought a BMW X5 for Less Than $4K in the States
17 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
And there’s obviously a catch, albeit a quite small one, because it is obvious from the images shared below that we are dealing with the first-generation of the brand’s popular SUV.
The E53 BMW X5 was put together between 1999 and 2006, and it is estimated that almost half a million copies saw the light of day during this time. Production took place at the Greet factory in South Carolina in the United States of America, as well as at Toluca in Mexico. And because BMW owned the Rover Group during that time, the vehicle shared its nuts and bolts with the era’s Range Rover, namely the L322, as well as the E39 5 Series.
The powertrain family consisted a 3.0-liter straight-six, a pair of V8s, and diesel power for selected markets, and depending on the chosen assembly, you could get the original X5 with a five-speed manual, a six-speed manual, a pair of five-speed automatics, including one from ZF, and a ZF six-speed automatic transmission. The model measured 183.7 inches (4,666 mm) in length, 73.7 inches (1,872 mm) in width, and 69.3 inches (1,760 mm) in height, and had a 111 inches (2,819 mm) long wheelbase.
Pictured in the gallery is a 2005 BMW X5 3.0i, so it features the base powertrain of that era. The 3.0-liter straight-six made 228 horsepower (231 ps/170 kW) and 214 pound-feet (N300 m) of torque back when the SUV was still new, and in this case, everything is channeled to both axles through a six-speed manual transmission. The 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) took just under 8 seconds, and flat-out, it could do 130 mph (210 kph).
Photo: Cars&Bids This BMW X5 features the Cold Weather Package, the Premium Package, and the Rear Climate Package. Other stuff mentioned in the ad includes the roof rails, automatic climate control, and cruise control. It has a Jet Black exterior on top of a Truffle Brown cockpit, a clean Florida title, and was located in Osteen before changing hands.
Despite being born more than two decades ago, this BMW X5 has never been involved in an accident, the Carfax vehicle history report reveals. It also has no mileage discrepancies, and as you can assume, it has seen plenty of driving over the years. At the time of cataloging, the odometer read 205,600 miles (330,900 km).
There are some notable modifications on deck, such as the 20-inch wheels sourced from a 4.6is BMW X5, aftermarket high-flow exhaust mufflers, a resonator delete, an Xtrons head unit, a subwoofer, and new door speakers.
As for the known flaws, these include plenty of chips and scratches on the outside, wear on the steering wheel, seats, and other surfaces inside, a sagging headliner, an illuminated tire pressure monitoring light, check display warning triangles, and some rust on the rear subframe components. According to the seller, the hood cables are stretched, and the hood is unable to be opened.
The radiator of this BMW X5 is said to have been replaced, though no documentation was provided. The hood release cables are included in the sale, alongside two keys.
Photo: Cars&Bids The seller bought this ride in May 2026, adding some 6,000 miles (~10,000 km) since, and he put it up for sale, stating that he is moving out of state, and does not need such a roomy vehicle anymore.
As you already know, the 2005 model year BMW X5 in the 3.0i configuration sells for pennies on the dollar these days. Its value depends on the number of miles, the overall appearance, and how well it has been maintained over the years, and the trade-in value starts from well under $1,000. Private parties tend to sell it from $1,800 to $2,500, and dealer listings range from $3,000 to $5,000 on average for high-mileage examples, whereas low-mileage cars can exceed $10,000 at auction.
This old BMW X5 , with its straight-six engine and six-speed stick shift, which had over 205,000 miles on the odo at the time of cataloging, was listed for grabs as part of an online auction. The vehicle was advertised at the excitement of no reserve on Cars&Bids, and when the gavel hit the table late last week, on October 23, 2026, it ended up changing hands for less than $4,000, as mentioned in the title. In fact, the selling price was $3,970.
Mind you, it may be a high-mileage machine, and one that has quite a few issues, but for what it’s worth, it is still a lot of car for the money, and giving it some extra shine will clearly cost a pretty penny, but it’s not undoable. It’s also a pretty good off-roader, in case you forgot, and it’s also a nice family hauler. But if you would have encountered this BMW X5 in time, would you have paid just under $4K for it? Helsing's The AD-1 Inferno and AD-2 Ambush interceptors. (Helsing)
WASHINGTON — Helsing, Germany’s highest-profile defense tech startup, today announced a new air defense system and a pair of new interceptor missiles.
Dubbed Contra, the company is billing its design as an “AI-controlled autonomous air defence system designed to protect countries from scaled drone and missile attacks,” according to a press release . Helsing also claims the system can track and engage “hundreds or thousands of drone and missile threats at the same time.”
The company says Contra can integrate with existing air defense interceptors and counter-drone systems. However, the firm also rolled out two new, container-launched interceptor designs it hopes customers will purchase with Contra. The AD-1 Inferno is jet-powered, “capable of aerial loitering, swarming, and repeated re-engagements.” The AD-2 Ambush uses a solid-rocket motor and can reach Mach 2.5, with a 20 km (around 12.5 miles) range, per the release.
The company did not provide hard cost estimates for the two missiles, saying only that the price will “significantly [undercut] those of existing missile interceptors.” There is currently a major push across NATO nations for lower-cost interceptors, with Anduril , Lockheed Martin and CHAOS Industries all rolling out options in the last few weeks.
“Our AI links existing sensors and effectors in real time and adds our interceptors, AD-1 and AD-2,” Helsing President and co-Founder Niklas Köhlersaid in the announcement. “With jet and rocket propulsion, a low-cost all-weather radar seeker, and two independent European supply chains, they deliver autonomous fire superiority up to ten kilometres high – affordable and at industrial scale.”

A Tesla Cybertruck was pulled over while driving in Germany, a reminder that the vehicle is generally not legal on European roads.
The Tesla Cybertruck has attracted plenty of attention, mostly for its unconventional and polarizing look. For better or worse*, the car looks different than anything else on the road, and thus has been the target of all sorts of discussion (*it’s for worse).
But it’s not just the look of the car that’s unconventional. Because of that look, it also breaks several European rules, particularly those related to pedestrian protection (which was called out immediately upon reveal by many observers, including this author).
As a result, it does not have “type approval” in Germany. Even applications for individual exemptions have been denied because of the vehicle “deviates significantly” from requirements .
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The vehicle is also too large. In general, a “class B” license, the normal license you get for driving a car, allows you to drive a vehicle up to 3,500kg (7,716lb). The Cybertruck does weigh less than this, but this number refers to the “Gross Vehicle Weight,” or the maximum weight of the truck when laden with occupants and cargo, for which all trims of the Cybertruck exceed 3,500kg.
A Swedish driver ran up against this barrier when driving through Bavaria, near the town of Vaterstatten, Merkur.de reports (with the funny title “Tesla monster truck stopped on A99”). The driver was holding a class B license, like most drivers, whereas the police said that a C1 license allowing operation of a vehicle up to 7.5 tons would be required.
Tesla Cybertruck impounded in Germany. Black bars obscure personally identifiable information. Photo: Hohenbrunn police
The police did not allow the driver to continue on their journey. Vaterstatten is near the Southern border of Germany, so the Cybertruck might not have been on German roads for long… except the driver is Swedish, so if they drove all the way from Sweden, they would have spent quite a while on German roads before being stopped.
Top comment by Nutmac
Liked by 10 people
Cybertruck's sharp edges aren't safe for many American roads and pedestrians, either. Tesla needs to go back to the drawing board or cancel it altogether.
View all comments
(Interestingly, in the police photo above, there are black bars all over the vehicle. Germany has strict privacy laws and hides personally identifiable information in public photos. That normally wouldn’t be the case with the hood of a car, but the Cybertruck in question is wrapped and seems to have several logos on it, which the German police had to cover up. Companies often use Cybertrucks for advertising, as they attract so much attention and are therefore used as rolling billboards)
We’ve seen similar situations before in Europe, with an imported Cybertruck being seized in the UK , someone trying to smuggle two through Lithuania into Russia , and with the US Army warning servicemembers that the Cybertruck is not allowed in Germany .
Nevertheless a few people still manage to get Cybertrucks onto European roads, by getting individual approval from one country or another, then driving across borders. But even in cases like that, a story like this shows that drivers could open themselves up to trouble by driving this unapproved vehicle on European roads.

Image: Tesla
Tesla expanded its Robotaxi service area in Houston today, and it shaped the new geofence like a rocket. Plenty of people on X see something else in it, which is fair given the phallic Austin map Tesla posted in 2025.
It’s a cute nod to Houston’s space history. It’s also a service area drawn for a meme, and Robotaxi Tracker counts only 34 driverless Model Ys to cover it.
Tesla’s official Robotaxi account announced the expansion on X this morning with “Houston, we have liftoff” and a map comparing the old and new geofences:
Houston, we have liftoff Bigger service area now live pic.twitter.com/ps8fZmWpuP — Robotaxi (@robotaxi) October 26, 2026
When Tesla launched in Houston in April, the service covered a small zone of about 25 square miles in northwest Harris County, around Jersey Village, Willowbrook and a stretch of FM 1960. It was miles away from downtown Houston.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The new geofence turns that zone into the nose cone and adds a long body running southeast to downtown and Bellaire, where it flares out into fins. Pair that with “Houston, we have liftoff,” a riff on the famous Apollo 13 line, and the theme isn’t subtle.
Tesla has done this before
The problem is that a long rocket drawn diagonally across a map also looks a lot like something else, and Tesla has been here before. In July 2025, less than a month into the Austin pilot, Tesla expanded its Austin geofence into a shape that people immediately compared to a penis. Instead of shrugging it off, Elon Musk leaned in:
Bigger, longer and uncut 😂 https://t.co/VmAfkdndMI — Elon Musk (@elonmusk) July 14, 2025
That post got about 30 million views. It didn’t age great either. Days later, Waymo expanded its own Austin territory to 90 square miles and was running roughly 100 times more vehicles than Tesla, as we reported at the time . Tesla still had employees riding in every car back then.
Big map, small fleet
Robotaxi Tracker, which crowdsources sightings of Tesla’s Robotaxi vehicles, now lists Tesla’s Houston service area at about 254 square miles, roughly 10 times the launch zone.
The fleet hasn’t grown nearly as fast. The tracker counts 34 unsupervised Model Ys in Houston, up from 22 three months ago, and no Cybercabs yet. That works out to about one car for every 7.5 square miles.
That’s the same pattern we saw in Austin earlier this year, when Tesla expanded “Robotaxi” to the entire Austin metro with only ~20 vehicles . To be fair, Austin has since caught up: the tracker now counts 397 driverless vehicles there, more than half of them Cybercabs.
Waymo has run fully driverless rides there since February and roughly doubled its Houston service area to nearly 50 square miles in May, ahead of the World Cup.

it's just to signal that Tesla and SpaceX plan to merge. Same with the roadster event - it has nothing to do with an actual product. the roadster 2 is vaporware. The event's only purpose is to signal a merger. that's what this map is

Why? There’s no logic in making the service area in this shape. Why not just make it where you think it is safe and useful to operate? All for a joke? It makes no sense to me.
During Tesla’s earnings call last week, the company again made it clear that safety is its biggest bottleneck for Robotaxi expansion. Tesla still limits itself to lower-speed roads and avoids more complex environments; even train crossings have been an issue.
Because of that, geo-fenced areas only tell part of the story. You can now order a ride within this area, but that doesn’t mean Tesla can operate efficiently there. It is limited by the number of vehicles in operation at any given time and the routes those vehicles take. Otherwise, Tesla would have bigger exposure to potential crashes.

The U.S. Postal Service says it is ready for the holiday shipping rush and expects to improve upon its delivery performance during the 2025 peak season, when mail items and packages were delivered within 2.5 days on average compared to 2.8 days during the same period the prior year.
Between Oct. 1 and Dec. 31 U.S. Postal Service mail and package volumes will increase about 40% for the holiday season.
The carrier has hired more than 10,000 seasonal workers, down from 14,000 last year and from 40,000 just a few years ago. Since 2020, a combination of improved staffing, reduced supervisor vacancies and lowered overtime rates has resulted in a more stable workforce and reduced the need for temporary help, the carrier said in a news release on Thursday.
“We have been preparing all year for this peak season, and we have enough capacity to handle whatever comes our way,” Postmaster General David Steiner said.
Why It Matters: Peak season is when carriers are tested the most and can feel customer backlash if they aren’t prepared to handle the higher volumes.
The postal operator credits new technology, logistics planning and execution for its ability to efficiently handle the influx of mail. Last year, between Nov. 15 and Jan. 9, on-time delivery scores were higher in nearly all service categories, with the best scores being in last mile delivery for shipped and postal consolidators injecting pre-sorted freight at post offices with large back-end receiving facilities to skip upstream postal processing..
The Postal Service installed 164 sophisticated, automated package sorting machines at facilities around the country this year, part of a $40 billion investment plan begun in 2022 to transform the organization’s middle-mile network. It has added a total of 673 high-speed sorters so far, according to the announcement. The machines can handle more and larger parcels than previous-generation machines.
In fiscal year 2026, ending Sept. 30, the USPS opened 31 sorting and delivery centers and 10 regional processing and distribution centers that work in tandem with 35 local processing facilities. In total since 2022, the Postal Service has opened 182 S&DCs, 19 regional DCs and four standalone regional transfer hubs.
S&DCs were created to remove duplication and increase efficiency in a network that relied on more than 18,000 destination delivery units — post offices with receiving docks postal officials said are too small, ill-equipped and poorly maintained. The sorting hubs consolidate work once assigned to about 10 DDUs and use small sorter equipment that can process between 2,500 to 4,300 pieces per hour to serve upward of 200,000 customers daily.
A better tracking and reporting platform, introduced in 2025, is also helping increase package visibility. The tracking is nearly four times faster than the previous version, often providing updates within a minute of scanning, the USPS said. The platform is connected with other systems that allow customers to get accurate information about the location of their packages using the USPS app or by signing up for messages.

S&DCs bring focus and structure to a network that for too long has relied on a haphazard and ever-growing patchwork of destination delivery units (DDUs), many of which are too small, ill-equipped and poorly maintained. With nearly 19,000 DDUs across the country, we were not only operating a costly delivery network but also perpetuating a system that has hindered our ability to evolve with the market as demand for package delivery soared.
The answer to this problem is our new system of S&DCs. Each of these large, spacious, well-equipped facilities — many already owned by the Postal Service or on a long-term lease — typically consolidate the work once assigned to about 10 DDUs. Each S&DC will use the latest automated sorting equipment to serve upward of 200,000 customers daily, bringing new efficiencies to our delivery operation and improving our service performance.
New commercial chief
To improve strategic planning in targeted markets, the quasi-private organization created a Chief Solutions and Strategy Office to analyse the entire enterprise, centralize network planning and identify ways to work more effectively and efficiently. The group is also working more closely with USPS customers to better match their needs with postal solutions, the Postal Service said.
In related news, the Postal Service earlier this month promoted Gary Reblin to chief commercial officer. He has served as chief technology officer since August 2025 after moving up the ranks for 35 years. In a LinkedIn message, Reblin said insights he gained as CTO will help decision making to modernize sales, competitive pricing for parcels, retail stores, delivery and tracking.
Reblin is credited with helping shape the early partnerships that brought privately transported parcels directly to local post offices for delivery, which continue to serve as an area of revenue growth for the financially struggling organization.

AI
Workstation
Workstation Processors
ASRock AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 Creator-Top 1
Thanks to the explosion in demand for AI inference hardware, high-end video cards have become a hot commodity in the PC parts market. This spike has affected video cards at almost every level, but it has hit workstation-grade cards hardest. The crème de la crème of cards, and, importantly, the ones that ship with the most VRAM, have been hit hardest. NVIDIA, AMD, and even Intel have felt this spike in demand, as discrete video cards have become the most effective way to add high-performance inference hardware to a standard-form-factor PC.
As part of our overall look at AI inference hardware and performance here at ServeTheHome, we have covered everything from mini-PCs to server-grade hardware , but not much in between. So today we are taking a look at that middle with a Radeon Pro AI workstation card from ASRock, their Creator Radeon AI Pro R9700. This is the fastest and best-equipped tier of workstation cards from AMD’s current-generation RDNA 4 architecture family.
The Radeon AI Pro R9700 is the latest in AMD’s long-running line of workstation cards. While it is a video card through and through, with cutting-edge graphics features and numerous display outputs, AMD knew where the market was headed when it released its latest generation of workstation cards and named them accordingly, putting AI capabilities front and center. The underlying architecture reflects that, with RDNA 4 adding a slew of AI-centric upgrades, including faster matrix math performance and support for lower-precision formats down to FP8. As a result, the R9700 is AMD’s most AI-capable workstation video card yet, and has arrived at a time when those capabilities are in very high demand.
If you want to check current prices or find one online, here is an Amazon Affiliate link .
ASRock Creator Radeon Pro AI R9700 Hardware Overview
As AMD is not selling their own reference design workstation cards for this generation, it falls to AMD’s partners to sell the cards instead. This production strategy is familiar to AMD on the consumer side, but it is a bit more unusual for a workstation card.
Most notably, AMD has kept its Radeon Pro partners on a rather short leash with card designs. AMD is curating a very specific image for a very specific market, chief among them the ability to install multiple cards in a single workstation. As a result, though AMD isn’t selling its reference card, its partner cards are all quite similar in high-level design: dual-slot blowers, a form factor you will not readily find outside workstation cards these days.
Xidax System-AMD Radeon AI Pro 3 Large
That brings us to ASRock’s Creator Radeon Pro AI R9700. ASRock has been a long-time partner of AMD’s at every level, from client and workstation motherboards to video cards. So it is not surprising to see them get into workstation video cards as well, now that AMD is offering that option to its closest partners.
ASRock AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 Creator-Top Angled 1
ASRock’s R9700 card is, in all practicality, exactly what you would expect from a workstation card given the form factor and AMD’s constraints. This dual-slot video card follows the PCIe specifications to a T in width and height to ensure it (and perhaps a few of its friends) fits in a workstation chassis.
ASRock Creator Radeon AI Pro R9700 Specifications
CUs | 64
AI Accelerators | 128
GPU Boost Clock Speed | 2.92GHz
Peak Matrix Throughput (FP8) | 382.7 TFLOPS
Peak Vector Throughput (FP32) | 47.8 TFLOPS
Memory | 32GB GDDR6
Memory Bandwidth | 640GB/sec (20Gbps x 256-bits)
ECC | Yes (Linux Only)
Infinity Cache | 64MB
I/O | PCIe Gen5 x16
TBP | 300W
Form Factor | PCIe CEM (Air Cooled)
Dimensions | 271 x 111 x 39 mm (10.7 x 4.4 x 1.5 in)
Architecture | RDNA 4
GPU | Navi 48
Under the hood, the card uses AMD’s Navi 48 GPU, the most powerful RDNA 4 GPU in this generation. The GPU offers 64 of AMD’s CUs, which in turn are comprised of a total of 4096 shading units for vector math and 128 AI accelerator cores for matrix operations.
Notably, AMD does not include discrete matrix math cores in the RDNA architecture as it does in its CDNA architecture. Instead, AMD relies on Wave Matrix Multiply-Accumulate (WMMA) for matrix operations, which run on the same CUs that make up the vector unit. Consequently, while these CU-integrated AI accelerators are not quite like the matrix hardware on AMD’s server-grade hardware, they are no slouch, either. Especially after AMD doubled its floating-point performance (and quadrupled its INT8 performance) coming from RDNA 3 to RDNA 4.
RDNA 4 Overview
With a peak clock speed of 2.92GHz, the R9700 delivers 382.7 TFLOPS of peak matrix math throughput with dense FP8 math, or double that with sparsity. One key improvement in this generation of RDNA architecture is added FP8 support, which not only boosts the card’s compute throughput but also better aligns AMD’s hardware with the industry trend toward lower-precision weights. While the card does not support faster execution of even lower precisions such as FP6 and FP4, it still supports them, as they are processed at FP8. The bigger benefit is that it still allows smaller weights and thus larger model parameter counts, making the most of the card’s 32GB of VRAM. The most typical example is to use FP6 weights to get a ~30B parameter model working on a 32GB card with some VRAM space to spare.
RDNA 4 Compute Engine
As is traditional for a workstation card, AMD and ASRock packed the R9700 with as much memory as the card can handle. With Navi 48 sporting a 256-bit bus, the card has 32GB of GDDR6 memory organized as 16 2Gbit chips in clamshell mode, meaning chips on the front and back of the card. Above all else, memory support is a key differentiator between AMD’s consumer and professional cards, so you will find 32 GB only on the Radeon AI Pro cards.
Patrick’s note : At an Advancing AI 2025 event, I asked AMD why the R9700 only had 32 GB. They looked at me like, why would you want more, since that is the max the memory configuration supports. My feedback was it might cost a lot more, but the market would probably absorb a higher cost and higher memory part for AI. I still wish AMD had something between this and the MI350P.
The GDDR6 memory clocks at 20Gbps, giving the card a total of 640GB/second of memory bandwidth. Meanwhile, as a workstation card, the R9700 has another ace up its sleeve: ECC support. This is implemented as soft ECC and is only available under Linux (and even then, it must be manually enabled), but it adds an extra layer of reliability for systems and racks built around the card. Again, with the ability to install up to 4 in standard ATX systems, the need for reliability increases because the odds of failure rise, so it is not just a checkbox feature.
AMD-Navi-48-Die-Shot
Navi 48 sits somewhere between a mid- to high-end GPU in die size (357mm2) and transistor count (53.9B), which makes it a bit of an oddity in AMD’s lineup as far as card progression goes. AMD did not produce a true high-end GPU this generation, and as a result, the R9700 actually has less VRAM than the previous-generation 48GB Radeon Pro W7900. This means it is a step back in overall memory capacity, but AMD is looking to make up the difference with compute throughput, thanks in large part to the newer chip architecture.
One advantage of being a smaller chip, however, is that it keeps TDPs in check. AMD (and ASRock’s) Total Board Power figure for the card is just 300 Watts, which makes it relatively easy to cool a blower-style card without a noise blowout. This also means that even 4 cards in a system is not going to result in excessive power requirements, though it will certainly be pushing the limits of a single power supply.
ASRock Creator Radeon Pro AI R9700 Build and Design
As for video card design, ASRock’s Creator Radeon AI Pro R9700 is a typical dual-slot blower design. To ensure the card can be installed in multiples, ASRock has kept things tightly tuned to PCIe specifications, with a dual-slot card measuring 10.7 inches long and 4.4 inches high.
Interestingly, the blower design here is open-backed, meaning the back side of the card has open vents so it can pull in air from both sides.
ASRock AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 Creator-Top 2
The fan itself is a pretty typical blower design. A single radial blower sits at the rear of the card, pushing cool air over the heatsink and toward the card’s PCIe bracket, where a large vent exhausts the resulting hot air. According to ASRock, it uses a vapor chamber to efficiently pull heat from the Navi 48 GPU, with a layer of Honeywell’s PTM7950 as the thermal interface material between the GPU and cooler.
Focusing on the rear of the card, we can better see the venting cut into the card’s PCB and its shroud. We can also see that the card has a shroud on its back side. As noted earlier, the 32GB of GDDR6 is organized in a clamshell configuration on the R9700, meaning 8 chips are on the rear of the card and need protection and cooling, just like the chips on the front side.
ASRock AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 Creator-Rear 1
Since this is a workstation card, ASRock has also put thought into its power connector placement. The Creator R9700 uses an ATX 12V-2×6 connector, placed on the rear of the card instead of the top, another workstation-centric design element that makes it easier to install multiple cards in a system. The 12V-2×6 connector is rated for up to 600W, so the 300W TBP R9700 is well within the cable’s limits.
ASRock AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 Creator-Front 1
Meanwhile, at the front of the card, you will find a not-too-subtle reminder that this is a video card, with 4 display outputs, the maximum the Navi 48 GPU can drive. Unique among R9700 vendors, ASRock went with an all-DisplayPort configuration, forgoing the usual HDMI port for a fourth DisplayPort. All DisplayPorts are DisplayPort 2.1a, and with DSC, the card can drive displays up to 12 K.
ASRock AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 Creator-Front Angled 2
Otherwise, aside from the display outputs, the rest of the front of the card is almost entirely vent cutouts. 300W is still a lot of heat for a blower card, so ASRock does not hold back, and you can clearly see the heatsink fins running through the card.
With our hardware tour complete, let us take a look at the performance of the Creator R9700.
